title: finding(ci): a corepack pnpm download failure reds the required `README Export Check` before the gate runs — on the merge_group leg that is a 60-minute queue stall
body:
**Finding (observation, awaiting first grading).** Filed unassigned and unlabelled by the `domain:skills` execution seat of #7728 / #7770 (PR #8091), from that run's out-of-scope report. No code was changed for this card and the seat does not grade or route it.

## What happened

On PR #8091 (a one-file `skills/**` prose diff), the required check **README Export Check** went **red 10 seconds into the job**, before any gate logic ran. Job https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectui/actions/runs/34041702654/job/101509535650, head `3916de68`, started 15:14:59Z, completed 15:15:09Z. The whole failure is the `corepack enable` step downloading pnpm:

```text
! Corepack is about to download https://registry.npmjs.org/pnpm/-/pnpm-10.31.0.tgz
node:internal/assert/utils:77
    throw err;
    ^
AssertionError [ERR_ASSERTION]: The expression evaluated to a falsy value:

  assert(!this.paused)

    at Parser.finish (node:internal/deps/undici/undici:6165:9)
    at TLSSocket.(anonymous) (node:internal/deps/undici/undici:6499:36)
    at TLSSocket.emit (node:events:531:35)
    at endReadableNT (node:internal/streams/readable:1698:12)
```

`rerun_failed_jobs` on the same head made it green with no code change, which is the evidence that it is the download and not the diff: same commit, same gate, opposite conclusion.

## Why this is worth a card and not just a re-run

The workflow's own header states both halves of the cost:

- `scripts/dependabot-merge-gate.mjs` classifies `README Export Check` as a **required context**, and since objectui#6160 the `merge_group` floor DERIVES from that same list.
- The header's own words for what a required check that fails on a queue build costs: "A required check that does not report on a queue build stalls the queue until the ruleset's 60-minute timeout fails it."

So this failure mode is not "one agent re-runs a job". On the `merge_group` leg it is a 60-minute queue stall triggered by a transient registry read, and the agent who sees it has to first prove the red is not theirs — which for a markdown-only diff means fetching the job log, which is itself behind an egress-blocked host for container seats (`productionresultssa11.blob.core.windows.net` is denied, so REST log download returns HTTP 000 and only the MCP `get_job_logs` path answers).

`corepack enable` is not local to this workflow: **15 of the workflows under `.github/workflows/` run it**, so the same blip can red any of them.

## Shape of a fix (for triage, not ruled)

Not investigated beyond the observation. The obvious directions, in the order a triage seat would probably weigh them:

1. Cache or pin the pnpm tarball so a job does not reach the registry at all on the hot path (`actions/setup-node`'s `cache: 'pnpm'` is already set in this workflow, but it caches the pnpm STORE, not the corepack-downloaded pnpm binary itself).
2. `pnpm/action-setup`, which resolves pnpm through its own cached path.
3. Retry only the setup step, which treats the symptom and leaves the 60-minute queue-stall exposure in place.

## Dedup

Searched with MCP `search_issues` (this seat's REST `/search/issues` is 403: "sessions are bound to their configured repositories"; repo-scoped REST reads work). The query returned three live results — #6392, #6358, #5246 — so it is a real reading and not an empty channel. All three are **closed** and about other things (a leftover `corepack enable` in a job that never installs; `changelog.yml`'s missing corepack setup; no workflow running `pnpm check`). No open card covers a corepack download failure reddening a required context. ⚠️ Bounded reading, not exhaustive.
